points.title: 童年与音乐启蒙
points.description: 18989月26日，乔治·格什温出生于纽约布鲁克林的一个俄罗斯犹太移民家庭。原名雅各布·格申维茨（Jacob Gershowitz）。他的父母莫里斯和罗丝·格什温是贫穷的移民，父亲在纽约经营一家小生意。格什温的早期音乐教育并不系统，直到1910年，他12岁时，听到朋友哥哥演奏钢琴后，才对音乐产生浓厚兴趣。1912年，他开始师从汉克·亨伯格学习钢琴，并展现出非凡的音乐天赋。这段时期，他接触到了纽约多元化的音乐文化，包括爵士乐、流行歌曲和古典音乐，为他后来的创作奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born on September 26, 1898, in Brooklyn, New York, to Russian Jewish immigrant parents Morris and Rose Gershowitz (later Americanized to Gershwin). His family was poor, and his father ran a small business. Gershwin's early musical education was informal until 1910, when at age 12, he developed a strong interest in music after hearing a friend's brother play piano. In 1912, he began studying piano with Hambauer and showed exceptional musical talent. During this period, he was exposed to New York's diverse musical culture, including jazz, popular songs, and classical music, which laid the foundation for his later compositions.

points.title: Tin Pan Alley 与早期创作
points.titleEn: Tin Pan Alley and Early Compositions
points.description: 1914年，16岁的格什温辍学，开始在纽约的 Tin Pan Alley 担任钢琴演奏员和歌曲推销员。他在杰里姆·H·雷米克音乐公司工作，为来访的顾客演奏最新的流行歌曲。这段经历让他深入了解了流行音乐的创作和商业运作。1916年，他创作了第一首商业成功的歌曲《When You Want 'Em You Can't Get 'Em, When You Got 'Em You Don't Want 'Em》。1918年，他的第一首流行歌曲《Swanee》由歌手艾尔·乔森演唱，大获成功，使格什温一举成名。在此期间，他还创作了多部百老汇音乐剧，如《拉拉露西尔》(1919)和《宝贝》(1920)，逐渐在纽约音乐界站稳脚跟。
points.descriptionEn: In 1914, at age 16, Gershwin dropped out of school and began working as a piano player and song plugger in New York's Tin Pan Alley. He worked for Jerome H. Remick & Co., playing the latest popular songs for visiting customers. This experience gave him deep insight into the creation and business of popular music. In 1916, he wrote his first commercially successful song, 'When You Want 'Em You Can't Get 'Em, When You Got 'Em You Don't Want 'Em.' In 1918, his first hit pop song 'Swanee,' performed by Al Jolson, became a massive success, catapulting Gershwin to fame. During this period, he also wrote several Broadway musicals, such as 'La La Lucille' (1919) and 'Lady, Be Good!' (1920), establishing himself firmly in New York's music scene.

points.title: 爵士交响与百老汇巅峰
points.description: 1924年是格什温职业生涯的转折点。他创作了融合爵士乐元素的交响乐《蓝色狂想曲》，由保罗·怀特曼指挥在纽约首演，获得巨大成功。这部作品打破了古典音乐与爵士乐之间的界限，使格什温成为美国音乐创新的代表人物。同年，他与兄弟艾拉·格什温合作创作了音乐剧《女士，好！》，其中的歌曲如《The Man I Love》和《Fascinating Rhythm》成为经典。1925年，他创作了《钢琴协奏曲》，进一步探索古典与爵士的融合。1926年，他的音乐剧《噢，女士！》和《我歌唱你》相继上演，巩固了他在百老汇的地位。这一时期，格什温频繁往返于纽约和欧洲，与当时著名的音乐家如拉威尔、斯特拉文斯基等人交往，不断拓展自己的音乐视野。
points.descriptionEn: 1924 marked a turning point in Gershwin's career. He composed 'Rhapsody in Blue,' a symphony incorporating jazz elements, which premiered in New York under Paul Whiteman's direction to great success. This work broke the barrier between classical and jazz music, establishing Gershwin as a pioneer of American musical innovation. The same year, he collaborated with his brother Ira on the musical 'Lady, Be Good!', featuring songs like 'The Man I Love' and 'Fascinating Rhythm' that became classics. In 1925, he wrote the 'Piano Concerto,' further exploring the fusion of classical and jazz. In 1926, his musicals 'Oh, Kay!' and 'Funny Face' premiered, solidifying his position on Broadway. During this period, Gershwin frequently traveled between New York and Europe, associating with prominent musicians like Ravel and Stravinsky, continuously expanding his musical horizons.

points.title: 国际声誉与电影音乐
points.description: 1928年，格什温首次前往巴黎，在那里创作了《一个美国人在巴黎》，这部作品融合了法国印象派和美国爵士元素，成为他最受欢迎的作品之一。在巴黎期间，他曾向著名作曲家纳迪亚·布朗热学习作曲技巧，尽管这段学习时间不长，但对他的创作产生了深远影响。1929年，格什温开始涉足好莱坞，为电影创作配乐，包括《随我起舞》(1930)和《 Shall We Dance》(1937)。1930年代，他创作了多部重要的百老汇音乐剧，如《Of Thee I Sing》(1931)，这是第一部获得普利策戏剧奖的音乐剧。1935年，他创作了美国第一部民谣歌剧《波吉与贝丝》，这部作品融合了爵士、蓝调和民间音乐元素，被视为他艺术成就的巅峰之作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1928, Gershwin traveled to Paris for the first time, where he composed 'An American in Paris,' a work blending French impressionism with American jazz elements, becoming one of his most popular pieces. During his Paris stay, he briefly studied composition with renowned Nadia Boulanger, which, though short-lived, profoundly influenced his creative approach. In 1929, Gershwin began working in Hollywood, composing film scores including 'Delicious' (1930) and 'Shall We Dance' (1937). In the 1930s, he created several important Broadway musicals, such as 'Of Thee I Sing' (1931), the first musical to win the Pulitzer Prize for Drama. In 1935, he composed 'Porgy and Bess,' America's first folk opera, blending jazz, blues, and folk elements, considered his artistic masterpiece.

points.title: 晚年创作与英年早逝
points.description: 1935年后，格什温主要在洛杉矶工作和生活，继续为好莱坞创作电影音乐。1936年，他开始创作《弦乐随想曲》，这是他最后一部大型管弦乐作品。然而，1937年7月9日，格什温在好莱坞因脑部肿瘤手术并发症去世，年仅38岁。他的突然离世震惊了整个音乐界，使人们更加认识到他短暂而辉煌的艺术成就。格什温的早逝使许多未完成的作品无法完成，包括他计划创作的交响曲。尽管生命短暂，格什温在不到20年的创作生涯中，创作了大量影响深远的作品，将美国民间音乐、爵士乐与欧洲古典音乐传统完美融合，开创了美国音乐的新时代。
points.descriptionEn: After 1935, Gershwin primarily worked and lived in Los Angeles, continuing to compose film scores for Hollywood. In 1936, he began working on 'Variations on I Got Rhythm,' his last major orchestral work. However, on July 9, 1937, Gershwin died in Hollywood from complications following brain tumor surgery at the age of 38. His sudden death shocked the music world, making people more aware of his brief but brilliant artistic achievements. Gershwin's early death left many unfinished works, including a planned symphony. Despite his short life, in less than 20 years of creative activity, he produced numerous influential works that perfectly merged American folk music, jazz, and European classical traditions, pioneering a new era in American music.

supporter.zh: 格什温是美国音乐史上最具创新精神的作曲家之一，他成功地将爵士乐和流行音乐元素融入古典音乐形式，创造了独特的美国音乐语言。他的作品如《蓝色狂想曲》和《波吉与贝丝》打破了高雅艺术与大众文化之间的界限，使美国音乐获得了国际认可。格什温的音乐充满活力、节奏鲜明，体现了美国多元文化的融合，为后来的作曲家如伯恩斯坦和科普兰开辟了道路。他短暂而辉煌的职业生涯展示了美国艺术家的创造力和才华，是美国文化自信的重要象征。
supporter.en: Gershwin stands as one of America's most innovative composers, successfully integrating jazz and popular music elements into classical forms to create a unique American musical language. His works like 'Rhapsody in Blue' and 'Porgy and Bess' broke barriers between high art and popular culture, earning American music international recognition. Gershwin's music, vibrant and rhythmically dynamic, reflects the fusion of America's diverse cultures, paving the way for later composers like Bernstein and Copland. His brief but brilliant career showcases the creativity and talent of American artists, symbolizing American cultural confidence.

critic.zh: 批评者认为格什温的作品在结构上存在不足，他的古典作品有时被指责为过于依赖爵士元素而缺乏真正的古典深度。一些评论家认为他的音乐技巧不够精湛，特别是在和声和配器方面。此外，格什温对非裔美国人音乐元素的运用，如在《波吉与贝丝》中，也引发了关于文化挪用的争议。他的早逝使许多潜在的发展方向无法实现，人们只能猜测如果他活得更久，他的艺术风格会如何演变。批评者还指出，格什温虽然成功地将美国音乐元素引入主流，但未能完全摆脱欧洲古典传统的束缚。
critic.en: Critics argue that Gershwin's compositions have structural deficiencies, with his classical works sometimes criticized for relying too heavily on jazz elements without achieving true classical depth. Some commentators认为 his musical technique was not sufficiently refined, particularly in harmony and orchestration. Additionally, Gershwin's use of African American musical elements, as in 'Porgy and Bess,' has sparked controversy about cultural appropriation. His early death prevented the realization of many potential directions, leaving us to speculate how his style might have evolved had he lived longer. Critics also note that while Gershwin successfully introduced American musical elements into the mainstream, he未能完全摆脱 European classical traditions.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，格什温被视为美国音乐现代化的关键人物，他代表了20世纪美国文化自信的崛起。他的作品成为美国国家身份的象征，特别是在《蓝色狂想曲》中，他将爵士乐提升到了艺术高度。格什温的音乐跨越了古典与流行、高雅与通俗的界限，影响了从电影配乐到流行音乐等多个领域。在流行文化中，他的旋律被广泛引用和改编，成为美国文化遗产的一部分。历史学家认为，格什温的成就不仅在于他个人的创作才华，更在于他成功地将美国多元文化融合为独特的艺术表达，为美国音乐赢得了国际地位。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Gershwin is regarded as a pivotal figure in American musical modernization, representing the rise of American cultural confidence in the 20th century. His works have become symbols of American national identity, particularly 'Rhapsody in Blue,' which elevated jazz to an art form. Gershwin's music transcended boundaries between classical and popular, highbrow and lowbrow, influencing fields from film scores to popular music. In popular culture, his melodies are widely quoted and adapted, becoming part of American cultural heritage. Historians believe that Gershwin's significance lies not only in his individual creative talent but in his successful fusion of America's diverse cultures into unique artistic expressions, earning American music international recognition.

self.zh: 音乐是自由的，它不应该被任何规则所束缚。
self.en: Music is free, it should not be bound by any rules.

others.zh: 格什温是唯一能够将爵士乐提升到艺术高度而不失去其本质的作曲家。
others.en: Gershwin is the only composer who could elevate jazz to an art form without losing its essence.
